::: {.why}
The store already carries an ingestion time, but the signal path does not use it, and a lag convention that lives in your head is one you will violate the first time you write a new signal.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State your lag convention explicitly: what is known at what time, and when a position computed from it can first be held.
- Show what a one-day error in that convention does to your pairs strategy's Sharpe.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Write the convention down as a table: for each data source, the timestamp of the observation, the timestamp of availability, and the first session in which a position derived from it can be held. Then encode it as a per-source lag in the store rather than as a shift in each notebook.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Measure the sensitivity: run your pairs strategy with the correct lag, with no lag, and with two days of lag. Report the three Sharpe ratios. The no-lag version will look substantially better, and the size of that gap is a measure of how much of your result is timing rather than signal.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add an assertion to the signal path: any position series must be derivable from data whose availability timestamp precedes the session it is held in, checked rather than intended.
:::
:::

:::
